## Pull request overview

> [!NOTE]
> Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review.

Prepares the monorepo for npm release readiness by standardizing package publishing metadata and aligning documentation to reflect the full 42-package inventory.

**Changes:**
- Normalized many `package.json` files with consistent publishing metadata (repo/homepage/bugs/keywords/files/engines/publishConfig).
- Added/rewrote several package READMEs to a canonical structure and added a new internal README template/checklist.
- Updated docs site pages + root docs/release notes/changelog to reflect 42 packages and include missing package entries.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 60 out of 60 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.

<summary>Comments suppressed due to low confidence (1)</summary>

**packages/services/service-tenant/package.json:1**
* This PR aims for consistent publishing metadata, but `author` here is `"ObjectStack Team"` while many other packages in the diff use `"ObjectStack"` (and the internal checklist calls for `"ObjectStack"`). Aligning `author` across packages will avoid unnecessary diff churn later and keep npm listing metadata uniform.
</details>

The checklist declares a per-package `homepage` (e.g. `/docs/packages/<slug>`) and a canonical `files` whitelist that includes `LICENSE`, but the updated `package.json` diffs in this PR generally set `homepage` to `https://objectstack.ai/docs` and `files` to `["dist", "README.md"]`. To avoid future “failing the checklist” confusion, either (a) update this template to match the repository’s chosen defaults, or (b) adjust the package metadata to satisfy the checklist (per-package homepage URLs + include `LICENSE` in the published files list).

To avoid future “failing the checklist” confusion, either (a) update this template to match the repository’s chosen defaults, or (b) adjust the package metadata to satisfy the checklist (per-package homepage URLs + include `LICENSE` in the published files list).

The `files` whitelist omits `LICENSE`, which can cause published tarballs to lack the actual license text (some compliance/security scanners expect it even when `license` is set). Consider adding `"LICENSE"` to `files` here (and consistently across publishable packages), especially since the internal publishing template in this PR lists it as canonical.

This example references `dispatcher` without defining/importing it, so it won’t copy/paste run as written. Consider either (a) showing how to construct the `dispatcher` (and where it comes from), or (b) adjusting the snippet to pass the correct concrete type/value expected by `registerRoutes` (e.g., the specific server/adapter integration object used by this package).
